title: Blindness in Dogs: Signs, Causes, Sudden Vision Loss and Care
description: Blindness in dogs: early signs your dog is going blind, common causes, when sudden blindness is an emergency, what's reversible and how to help a blind dog.
secondaryKeywords: how to tell if my dog is going blind

faq.q: How can I tell if my dog is going blind?
faq.a: Watch for hesitation on stairs or before jumping, clinginess or anxiety in new places, startling easily, slower walks and less eye contact. Bumping into furniture often appears only once vision is nearly gone, so see your vet early.

faq.q: What causes sudden blindness in dogs?
faq.a: Common causes include acute glaucoma, retinal detachment, SARDS, a severe corneal ulcer and optic nerve disease. Sudden vision loss, with or without pain, needs a vet right away.

faq.q: Can blindness in dogs be reversed?
faq.a: Sometimes. Cataract surgery can restore vision, and emergency treatment for acute glaucoma can sometimes save sight. Progressive retinal atrophy and SARDS have no effective treatment.

faq.q: Can diabetes make a dog blind?
faq.a: Yes, through cataracts that often form quickly. In one study of diabetic dogs, half had cataracts within 170 days of diagnosis, so regular eye checks matter.

faq.q: Can a blind dog have a good quality of life?
faq.a: Yes. If the eyes aren't painful, most dogs adapt well using smell and hearing, especially with a consistent home layout, gated stairs and verbal cues.
